bullets.title: NVDA guides ~70% FY28 revenue growth vs. 45% consensus, triggers broad PT upgrades
bullets.body: Nvidia's Q2 print showed FY2028 revenue guidance of ~70% YoY growth vs. the 45% consensus, with BofA noting 'demand still exceeds supply.' Wall Street responded with a flurry of PT raises: Bernstein to $400, BofA Buy/$350, Melius to $420, JPMorgan to $320, Goldman to $300 (but flagged 'elevated expectations could keep shares range-bound near-term'). CFO Colette Kress confirmed the company is working to close the supply-demand gap.

bullets.title: AWS + NVIDIA commit 2M additional GPUs for 2027-28; Google/NVDA adding ~45GW compute
bullets.body: AWS and NVIDIA announced 2 million additional GPU commitments for 2027 and 2028, spanning Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, Rubin Ultra, and Vera CPU architectures. Separately, Google and Nvidia together are expected to add approximately 45GW of compute capacity next year, underscoring the depth of the AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: SPX pricing 35bps volatility for Warsh Jackson Hole speech; Nasdaq vol back to investable
bullets.body: One trader notes NVDA earnings 'put a bid into tech' but the market's real focus is Fed Chair Warsh's 10AM ET speech Friday, with SPX implying an additional 35bps of movement. A dovish/neutral Warsh would shift attention to 8,000 SPX support into September OPEX. Separately, Nasdaq volatility is moving 'back into the investable bucket' post-NVDA.

bullets.title: NVDA expected to break all-time highs; shorts to cover quickly, underweight longs lag
bullets.body: One fintwit account with a track record on NVDA calls argues the stock will break all-time highs, with funding shorts forced to cover quickly while underweight long-only managers will take longer to reposition. NVDA's average post-earnings move is 7.4% across the last 12 reports vs. 2.75% over the past 8 quarters.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings lift NDX +1.0%, SPX +0.4%; other Mag 7 names softer in premarket
bullets.body: Tech rallied sharply on NVDA's guidance beat (SPX +0.4%, NDX +1.0%), easing AI spending slowdown fears. However, other Mag 7 names were broadly lower in premarket: AAPL -1.1%, GOOGL -0.4%, AMZN -0.3%, suggesting the NVDA lift is stock-specific rather than a broad AI re-rating.

bullets.title: Analyst skepticism on NVDA visibility: 'circular deal announcements' and AI headline fatigue
bullets.body: At least one analyst flags 'Jensen's constant visibility this quarter, the myriad of circular deal announcements' as a concern, suggesting investors should apply more scrutiny to whether announced AI deals represent genuine incremental demand or headline recycling.

bullets.title: Broadcom enabling OpenAI's 'Jalapeño' custom inference chip
bullets.body: Broadcom is reportedly enabling OpenAI's first custom inference chip, codenamed 'Jalapeño,' which could disrupt the competitive hardware landscape for AI accelerators.

bullets.title: META holds compute surplus, can monetize excess inference capacity to third parties
bullets.body: One account argues META 'is in a perfect negotiating position' given it holds excess compute capacity relative to current inference demand while the broader industry faces a compute shortage. META could sell excess fleet capacity to external customers, creating a new revenue stream.

bullets.title: META planning first KRW-denominated bond issuance in South Korea (≥1T won)
bullets.body: Korea Economic Daily reports Meta is seeking to issue Korean won-denominated bonds worth at least KRW 1 trillion — marking the first time a U.S. mega-cap tech company has tapped the KRW corporate bond market.

bullets.title: EU Commission orders META to improve screen time management and parental controls
bullets.body: EU Commission spokesperson issued a directive requiring Meta to enhance screen time management features and strengthen parental oversight capabilities, adding to the regulatory compliance burden on the platform.

bullets.title: Trump admin weighing new semiconductor tariffs; potential expansion to laptops and servers
bullets.body: Politico reports the White House is weighing a new round of tariffs on chips and is also considering expanding duties to laptops and servers. Policy could change and a phase-in period is reportedly under discussion — but the risk overhang is real for hardware supply chains.

bullets.title: AI basket repositioned from #1 to #2 weighting; NBIS/IREN relief rally expected but seen as short-lived
bullets.body: One account notes its AI basket was 'highest weighted' and has been reduced to second position. On the single-name side, NBIS and IREN are flagged for a relief rally today on NVDA's print, though the same author is 'skeptical the rally will be long-lived' given the macro backdrop.

bullets.title: S&P 500 EPS growth hits 52% YoY with 477 companies reported post-NVDA/CRWD
bullets.body: Post NVDA and CRWD prints, 477 of S&P 500 companies have now reported, showing YoY EPS acceleration of +52% — the strongest read since the 4Q21 post-pandemic rebound when corporate profits grew 27.9%.

bullets.title: Fed's Schmid: inflation 'stubborn and sticky,' rates not restraining economy
bullets.body: Fed's Schmid described inflation as 'stubborn and sticky' and said current interest rates are 'not restraining the US economy,' signaling a cautious near-term rate path. He separately said midterms won't affect the Fed's October meeting decision.

bullets.title: Dollar traders increasingly bullish ahead of Warsh Jackson Hole speech; USD options 57% bullish
bullets.body: Currency traders are building bullish dollar hedges ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech Friday, with 57% of dollar options flows this week favoring further USD gains vs. 43% last week. Markets are focused on whether Warsh will assert Fed independence.

bullets.title: ECB minutes signal pause; some members may have supported a rate hike
bullets.body: ECB records show labor market conditions have weakened (reducing second-round inflation risk), price pressures are easing, and recent data 'strongly supports a pause.' However, some ECB members might have supported a rate increase, and ECB's Radev said 'vigilance should prevail over patience' after September.

bullets.title: JPMorgan warns global food inflation to surge to 5% by early 2027 on Hormuz fertilizer crunch
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts global food inflation rising from 2.8% currently to 5% by early 2027, driven by Strait of Hormuz closure since February cutting off one-third of global nitrogen fertilizer supply. 41% of Americans now report concern about grocery affordability, up from 24% in April.

bullets.title: Qatar-Iran discuss phased Hormuz shipping corridor; Kuwait/Qatar ramping crude exports
bullets.body: Qatar and Iran are discussing a phased framework including a temporary shipping corridor and joint mine-clearing project in the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait and Qatar are also ramping crude flows through Hormuz as Oman-Iran talks ease supply fears, with Iraq separately offering oil outside Hormuz for the first time since the conflict began.

bullets.title: July macro data: PCE cools, corporate profits +22.8% YoY, savings rate rebounds to 3.0%
bullets.body: July showed supercore CPI and PCE both cooling toward the Fed's 2% target. Corporate profits surged 22.8% YoY in 2Q26 (highest since 4Q21). The personal savings rate bounced to 3.0% (4-month high), while core capital goods shipments rose +1.4% m/m (one of the strongest YTD reads). Services spending led with $86.2B gain vs. $49.9B decline in goods.

bullets.title: AMD and TSM charts flagged as 'looking strong'; buy dips thesis
bullets.body: One trader flagged both AMD and TSM as showing similar chart strength, recommending holding existing positions and adding on dips — a constructive semiconductor view complementary to the NVDA move.
